- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 30d forecast), especially if sentiment was bullish; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak observed in history.
- If 30d forecast shows strong upward trend but true outcome is flat or declines, apply mean reversion: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until trend flattens.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
- For low sentiment + low price history, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for potential rebound.
- If 30d forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 2–5% if sentiment is weak or neutral; otherwise, maintain unless sentiment turns bullish.
